source.publisher: Irish News (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed: the only nomination for the division in the Irish News list of the Dungannon Rural Council nominations (6 May 1936, p. 7), in which Granville is the only division with two candidates

note: Triennial election of the Dungannon rural district councillors, 1936. Nominations closed on 5 May 1936. The Irish News of 6 May 1936, p. 7 prints the nominations for all nineteen divisions: eighteen single nominations, returned unopposed, and Granville, where the Unionist, Mr. Wm. Hall, was opposed by Mr. Robert Newton, D.L., chairman of the Dungannon Ratepayers' Association (also Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1936, p. 15). The Nationalists did not nominate for Clonavaddy and Coalisland. The Granville result has not been found, so Granville is not recorded. Bernagh is held: the Mid-Ulster Mail (9 May 1936, p. 9) reports a possible contest there, which the Irish News list does not show. Labels are as printed. Polling in County Tyrone was fixed for Wednesday 3 June 1936. 'The Nationalists did not nominate candidates for Clonavady and Coalisland divisions, two of their strongholds, and Messrs. Brown and Watt have an unexpected walk-over.' Returned unopposed.
